title: NAS deploy: Dockerfile, compose + tailscaled sidecar, runbook
description:
## What to build

Deploy shape C to Wilde-NAS as a standalone compose stack with its own tailnet node, following the proven torhaus runbook pattern (`~/dev/torhaus/deploy/README.md` as the template; PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md, M6). Grilled decisions: standalone stack (not joined to torhaus compose), own Tailscale node via `tailscale/tailscale` sidecar (tsnet is Go-only, the Rust server can't embed it), own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` volume, same `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` value duplicated in this stack's env.

Image (multi-stage Dockerfile, linux/amd64 for the DS423+):

1. Frontend build stage: bun → vite `dist/`
2. Rust build stage: `thoughttree-server` release binary
3. Runtime stage: needs Node.js LTS + the ACP adapter chain the server spawns — `claude-code-acp` adapter and the Claude Code CLI (torhaus image proves Claude Code CLI headless-in-Docker works on this NAS; mirror its approach). Auth: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env (from `claude setup-token`), `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/claude` on a persistent volume.

Compose stack:

- `thoughttree-server`: env `TT_STORAGE=webdav`, `TT_WEBDAV_*`, `TT_DATA_DIR=/data` (volume, holds turn journal), `TT_LIST_ROOT=/vault` with the vault bind-mounted **read-only** (ADR 0004), `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/claude` (volume)
- `tailscale` sidecar: `tailscale/tailscale` image, `TS_AUTHKEY`, hostname `thoughttree`, tailscale serve → HTTPS to the server port (gives a clean `https://thoughttree.<tailnet>.ts.net` with valid certs for the PWA; service worker/PWA install requires HTTPS)
- No published host ports — reachable via tailnet only (v1 auth = tailnet membership, PRD assumption)

Runbook `deploy/README.md` in the repo, cloned from the torhaus structure: buildx build, image import into Container Manager, tagged versions + rollback procedure, log access, where secrets live, token rotation note (update env in both torhaus and thoughttree stacks).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docker buildx` produces a linux/amd64 image; stack runs on the DS423+ via Container Manager
- [ ] `https://thoughttree.<tailnet>.ts.net` reachable from iPad over Tailscale with valid TLS; PWA installs to home screen
- [ ] Full round-trip on iPad: browse vault, open graph, prompt, live stream, permission prompt, guarded save via WebDAV — and the saved change appears in Nextcloud sync clients
- [ ] Detached-turn flow works in production: lock iPad mid-stream, unlock later → replay/apply/ack
- [ ] Vault mount is read-only in the container (verified); no published host ports; secrets only in env/secret files, not in the image
- [ ] Runbook covers build, deploy, rollback, token rotation

## Blocked by

- Parked permissions end-to-end
- WebDAV vault backend

title: Parked permissions end-to-end (park, reattach-first surfacing, resume)
description:
## What to build

Parked permissions end-to-end (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md; CONTEXT.md: Parked permission): an agent permission request that fires while no client is attached pends indefinitely — no timeout, no auto-deny — pauses its Turn, and is the first thing a reattaching client sees.

Most machinery exists: core's `PermissionBroker` already parks requests and exposes `pending()`; the Turn registry tracks `TurnState::AwaitingPermission`. This issue wires it through the server protocol and the PWA UX:

- `ServerEventSink.permission_request` → broadcast `{ "type": "permission-request", "turnId": ..., ...PermissionRequestEvent }` to attached clients AND flip the Turn's state to `AwaitingPermission`.
- `AttachSnapshot.parkedPermissions` populated from `PermissionBroker::pending()` (scoped to the graph's active Turn).
- New endpoint: `POST /api/permissions/{requestId}` body `{ "optionId": "..." }` → `broker.respond` → 200 | 404 (unknown/already answered). `HttpTransport.respondToPermission` maps to it.
- Turn state returns to `Streaming` when the broker resolves the request.

PWA UX: on snapshot containing parked permissions, show the permission modal before anything else (PRD: "surfaced first on reattach"); while a permission is parked and the client is attached, the existing permission prompt UI is reused — same component as desktop, driven through the transport events. Answering resumes the stream live.

Desktop path must remain byte-identical (same broker; `TauriEventSink` + `respond_to_permission` command already delegate to it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Trigger a tool call requiring permission from the PWA, then detach all clients: Turn parks in `AwaitingPermission` (observable via journal/log or a state field on snapshot), no timeout fires
- [ ] Reattach: permission modal appears before any other UI action; approving resumes the Turn to completion; denying completes the Turn with the denied outcome
- [ ] Answering an already-answered/unknown request → 404, surfaced gracefully (modal dismisses)
- [ ] Two attached clients: both see the permission request; first answer wins, second gets the 404 path
- [ ] Desktop permission flow unchanged
- [ ] Tests: broker pending()-to-snapshot wiring; respond endpoint happy/404 paths

## Blocked by

- Server Turns (WS events, TurnRegistry, journal)

title: WebDAV vault backend: If-Match ETag CAS (spike first)
description:
## What to build

The WebDAV vault backend for shape C production: reads/list from the read-only NAS mount, writes through Nextcloud WebDAV with `If-Match` ETag as the compare-and-swap transport (ADR 0004: docs/adr/0004-guarded-project-writes.md). PRD flags ETag semantics as a named risk — so this issue starts with a timeboxed spike.

Spike first (record findings as comments on this issue before implementing):

1. `GET` a file via Nextcloud WebDAV — confirm response carries a usable ETag.
2. `PUT` with stale `If-Match` → expect 412; with current ETag → expect success + new ETag.
3. ETag stability: does the ETag change only on content change (vs. on sync/metadata events)?
4. Fallback decision if `If-Match` is unreliable: GET-hash-compare-PUT with narrower race window (documented, not silent).

Implementation — second `VaultStorage` impl in `thoughttree-core` (or a small `thoughttree-vault-webdav` module inside core; implementer's call, but it must stay MIT and behind the existing trait):

```rust
pub struct WebDavVault {
    http: reqwest::Client,
    base_url: url::Url,            // e.g. https://nas/remote.php/dav/files/{user}/{vault-subpath}/
    credentials: WebDavCredentials, // Nextcloud app password; from env, never logged
    /// Optional read-only bind mount of the same vault subtree, used ONLY for list()
    /// (fast directory walks). Reads use GET so content + ETag arrive atomically.
    list_root: Option<std::path::PathBuf>,
}
```

Semantics mapping (Revision = ETag here; callers can't tell — it's opaque):

- `read` → `GET` (content + ETag in one response; never read content from the mount and ETag from PROPFIND separately — that pairing races)
- `write` with `expected: Some(rev)` → `PUT` + `If-Match: <etag>`; 412 → `VaultError::Stale { current }` (fetch current ETag for the error)
- `write` with `expected: None` → plain `PUT`
- `list` → walk `list_root` if configured, else `PROPFIND Depth: infinity` (or per-dir Depth 1 walk if the server rejects infinity)

Server config: `TT_STORAGE=local|webdav`, `TT_WEBDAV_URL`, `TT_WEBDAV_USER`, `TT_WEBDAV_PASSWORD` (env only), optional `TT_LIST_ROOT`. Security: credentials never in logs or error strings; HTTPS enforced for non-localhost URLs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Spike findings (ETag behavior, 412 semantics, stability) recorded on the issue; fallback documented if needed
- [ ] `WebDavVault` implements `VaultStorage`; stale write surfaces as 409 `{ current }` through the server API, driving the same Reload/Overwrite UX
- [ ] Guarded write round-trip against a real Nextcloud instance verified (manual integration run acceptable; scriptable preferred); a write is immediately visible to other Nextcloud sync clients
- [ ] `list()` works via mount path and via PROPFIND fallback
- [ ] Credentials sourced from env, absent from logs/errors
- [ ] Unit tests with a mocked WebDAV server for read/write/stale/list

## Blocked by

- Guarded writes (VaultStorage trait)
- GATE: mobile-usage validation evidence

title: Server Turns: WS events, TurnRegistry, buffer+replay, turn journal + client apply
thoughttree-server skeleton (AGPL): axum, projects API, PWA serve, HttpTransport
description:
## What to build

The `thoughttree-server` crate (AGPL-3.0 from first commit — ADR 0005) plus the frontend `HttpTransport`, delivering the first browser-served slice: browse the Vault, open a graph, edit, guarded-save — the full project lifecycle over HTTP, no chat yet (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md, M4 start + M5 start).

Server: new workspace member `crates/thoughttree-server` (axum + tokio), consuming `thoughttree-core`'s `VaultStorage` (LocalFsVault for now; WebDAV backend is a separate issue — keep the storage choice behind config).

HTTP API v1 (JSON; single stale-write convention = 409):

```
GET  /api/health                → 200 { "status": "ok", "version": "..." }
GET  /api/projects              → 200 [ { "relativePath": "...", "modifiedEpochMs": ... } ]
GET  /api/projects/{*path}      → 200 { "content": "...", "revision": "..." } | 404
PUT  /api/projects/{*path}
     body: { "content": "...", "baseRevision": "..." | null }
     → 200 { "revision": "..." } | 409 { "current": "..." } | 400
POST /api/graphs/{*path}/prompt → 501 (stub until the Turns issue)
Static fallback: serve the built PWA (vite dist/), SPA fallback to index.html
```

Config via env (document in crate README): `TT_VAULT_ROOT` (required), `TT_BIND` (default `0.0.0.0:7420`), `TT_DATA_DIR` (for later turn journal). Auth: none — tailnet membership is the v1 perimeter (PRD assumption); bind is expected to sit behind Tailscale in deployment. Path handling must reuse core's vault path validation (no traversal).

Frontend: `HttpTransport` implements `BackendTransport` for the project surface (`loadProject`/`saveProject`/`listProjects` → the API above; `sendPrompt` rejects with a clear "not yet available" until the Turns issue; `capabilities.nativeDialogs = false`). Transport selection at boot: Tauri runtime detected → `TauriTransport`, else `HttpTransport` against same-origin `/api`. Project picker UI for the no-native-dialogs case: list from `listProjects()`, open on tap — this replaces the desktop open-dialog flow in the PWA. PWA manifest (standalone display, icons) so iPad can install it.

Stale-save UX (Reload/Overwrite dialog from the guarded-writes issue) must work identically through `HttpTransport` — the 409 body maps to `StaleRevisionError`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `crates/thoughttree-server` with AGPL-3.0 LICENSE file; workspace still builds; core stays MIT
- [ ] API endpoints behave as specified incl. 409-with-current-revision on stale writes and 404 on missing project; path traversal rejected
- [ ] Server serves the built frontend; SPA fallback works
- [ ] In a desktop browser and iPad Safari (LAN): list vault, open a graph, edit a node, save; concurrent edit → 409 → Reload/Overwrite dialog works
- [ ] PWA installable on iPad (manifest + icons)
- [ ] Rust integration tests for the projects API against a temp vault (axum + LocalFsVault)

## Blocked by

- Frontend transport seam (BackendTransport)
- Cargo workspace split (thoughttree-core)
- Guarded writes (VaultStorage)
- GATE: mobile-usage validation evidence

title: Guarded writes: VaultStorage trait, LocalFsVault CAS, stale-save UX
Cargo workspace split: crates/thoughttree-core + Tauri app crate
description:
## What to build

Split the Rust side into a cargo workspace so one core crate serves every deployment shape (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md, M2; CONTEXT.md: Deployment shape):

- `crates/thoughttree-core` — MIT (own LICENSE file). Contains the Tauri-free backend: `types`, `events` (SessionEventSink + event structs), `permissions` (PermissionBroker), `acp/{clients,process,sessions}`, `runtime` (LocalSet helper). Zero `tauri` dependencies — this is the crate a future axum server and the existing desktop shell both consume.
- The Tauri app crate — keeps `main.rs`/`lib.rs`, `commands/*`, `config.rs` (tauri_plugin_store stays here; core receives plain values, which is already true after the de-Tauri prefactor), `TauriEventSink`, `tauri.conf.json`, build script, bundling.

Layout constraint, not prescription: core must live outside the Tauri app crate under `crates/`; whether the app crate stays at `src-tauri/` (Tauri tooling default) or moves to `crates/thoughttree-tauri` is the implementer's call — pick whatever keeps `bun run tauri dev` and `bun run tauri:build` working with minimal config (`tauri.conf.json` build paths, sidecar bundling unchanged).

License boundary per ADR 0005 (docs/adr/0005): core is MIT; the workspace layout must make the (future) AGPL server crate boundary obvious — put a LICENSE file in each crate now.

Update CI/dev commands from CLAUDE.md (`cargo fmt/clippy/test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml`) to workspace form, and update CLAUDE.md itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cargo workspace with `crates/thoughttree-core` + Tauri app crate; `cargo test --workspace` passes
- [ ] `thoughttree-core` builds standalone and `cargo tree -p thoughttree-core` shows no `tauri` (enforced in CI or a test/script)
- [ ] `thoughttree-core` has an MIT LICENSE file
- [ ] `bun run tauri dev` and `bun run tauri:build` work; app identifier/bundle unchanged; zero user-visible change
- [ ] CLAUDE.md build commands updated to workspace paths

## Blocked by

- Backend de-Tauri prefactor (SessionEventSink + PermissionBroker)

title: GATE: mobile-usage validation evidence (remote-desktop stopgap)
description:
## What to build

Validation gate from the PRD (docs/prd/mobile-push.md, GATE after M3): before any server-side work starts, gather real evidence that mobile ThoughtTree usage is real — via the zero-code stopgap, remote desktop over Tailscale (Screens/Moonlight to the laptop running desktop ThoughtTree).

Not a code issue. Steps:

1. Set up remote desktop access from iPad to the Mac running ThoughtTree over Tailscale.
2. Use it for natural (not forced) ThoughtTree sessions for at least several days.
3. Record: number of real sessions, contexts (couch, travel, away-from-desk), what worked, what hurt (canvas interaction, text input, latency), and whether the pull to reach for it was real.
4. Decide go/no-go for the server milestones and record the decision + evidence summary in the PRD (Status line + short evidence note).

If usage is not real: stop the mobile push here — M1–M3 (GraphModel package, core extraction, guarded writes) already paid for themselves (PRD rationale).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Stopgap ran for a real usage period (not a one-off demo)
- [ ] Evidence summary recorded in docs/prd/mobile-push.md
- [ ] Go/no-go decision recorded; if go, server issues unblocked (this milestone closed)

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately (independent of code issues).

title: Backend de-Tauri prefactor: SessionEventSink trait + PermissionBroker
Frontend transport seam: BackendTransport interface + TauriTransport
Extract graph-model TS package (packages/graph-model)
description:
## What to build

Extract the pure graph domain layer out of `src/lib/graph/` into a standalone workspace package `packages/graph-model` (npm name `@thoughttree/graph-model`), consumed by the app exactly as before. This is the prefactor that lets the canvas PWA, a future thread view, and a future Obsidian plugin share one implementation of graph semantics (PRD: docs/prd/mobile-push.md, M1).

Scope decision — purity boundary: the package contains only the ReactFlow-free modules: `types`, `model` (GraphModel), `mutations` (GraphMutations), `serialize` (GraphSerialize, GRAPH_JSON_VERSION). The ReactFlow projection (`projection.ts`, `graphToFlowNodes`/`graphToFlowEdges`, `FlowNode` types) stays in the app — it is presentation (see CONTEXT.md "ReactFlow projection") and must not drag `@xyflow/react` into the package's dependency tree.

Public API of the package = the current ReactFlow-free exports:

```ts
// packages/graph-model — public surface
export { GraphModel } from './model'
export { GraphMutations } from './mutations'
export { GraphSerialize, GRAPH_JSON_VERSION } from './serialize'
export type { Graph, GraphEdge, GraphJSON, GraphNode, NodeId, Position } from './types'
```

Set up bun workspaces in the root `package.json` (`"workspaces": ["packages/*"]`). Move the module tests (`model.test.ts`, `mutations.test.ts`, `serialize.test.ts`) into the package. App code and `projection.ts` import from `@thoughttree/graph-model`. Domain vocabulary: CONTEXT.md (Graph, GraphNode, GraphModel, Conversation path).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `packages/graph-model` exists as a bun workspace package; app imports `@thoughttree/graph-model`, no imports of the old `src/lib/graph` model/mutations/serialize paths remain
- [ ] Package has zero runtime dependencies; `@xyflow/react` does not appear anywhere in the package (deps or imports)
- [ ] `projection.ts` remains in the app and imports domain types from the package
- [ ] `bun test:run` passes; package tests run from the package
- [ ] `bun run build` (typecheck + vite) passes; app behavior unchanged

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately.
